evals.prompt: Review my talk plan and tell me what I'm doing wrong: 40 slides, each is a bulleted list I'll read out loud, footnotes in 9pt font, our company logo and the conference name on every single slide, and I'll finish with a live coding demo to fill the last 15 minutes.
evals.expected_output: Names the specific antipatterns present (Bullet-Riddled Corpse, Ant Fonts, Floodmarks, Dead/Live Demo risk) and gives the catalog's remedies, ideally citing the relevant reference file.
expectations: Identifies the bulleted-read-aloud slides as the Bullet-Riddled Corpse antipattern
Identifies the 9pt footnotes as the Ant Fonts antipattern
Identifies the logo/conference-name on every slide as the Floodmarks antipattern
Flags the fill-time live demo as the Dead Demo antipattern and/or the Live Demo risk tradeoff
Names the antipatterns using the catalog's pattern names (not just generic advice)

evals.prompt: Help me plan a 45-minute conference talk introducing our new open-source caching library to backend engineers.
evals.expected_output: A phased plan grounded in the patterns: establish purpose and audience, structure before building slides, a narrative shape, a demo approach, and rehearsal.
expectations: Establishes purpose via the Big Why and researches the audience via Know Your Audience
Recommends structuring content before opening a slide tool (Fourthought: ideate/capture/organize/design)
Recommends a narrative shape such as Narrative Arc, Triad, or a Talklet series
Handles the demo deliberately (Lipsync or a Live Demo risk tradeoff rather than a naive live demo)
Recommends rehearsal (Carnegie Hall) and/or Brain Breaks appropriate to a 45-minute slot

evals.prompt: I get nervous during the Q&A part of my talks, I say 'um' a lot, and there's always one person who tries to derail me with hostile questions. Give me concrete techniques.
evals.expected_output: Delivery-phase techniques: repeat questions, embrace pauses over fillers, seed the first question / plant allies, and a heckler-handling method.
expectations: Recommends the Echo Chamber technique (repeat each question before answering)
Addresses filler words via Hiccup Words / Breathing Room (embrace purposeful pauses)
Suggests Seeding the First Question and/or a Posse to ease the Q&A
